chunks: O you who believe, stand up as witnesses for God in all fairness, and do not let the hatred of a people deviate you from justice. Be just: This is closest to piety; and beware of God. Surely God is aware of all you do.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about maintaining justice even when you hate a group of people?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for establishing 'Adl' (justice) as a core attribute of God and a primary duty for believers, extending beyond mere legal fairness to include impartiality in all social and political spheres. The phrase 'Qawwameena' implies those who stand firm and uphold justice even against personal bias or tribal loyalty, a concept deeply linked to the Ahl al-Bayt's role as just leaders. This commandment serves as a theological foundation for the Shia emphasis on objective truth over partisan allegiance.
